'''Guilherme Carvalho dos Santos''' (born 22 June 2002) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Professional career==
===Minas (2018–2022)===
Santos made his professional debut with [[Minas Tênis Clube (basketball)|Minas]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]] (NBB) during the [[2018–19 NBB season|2018–19]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fábrica de talentos|url=https://minastenisclube.com.br/noticias/basquete-formado-na-base-do-minas-gui-santos-esta-inscrito-no-draft/|website=MinasTenisClube.com.br|publisher=[[Minas Tênis Clube]]|date=23 April 2021|access-date=3 June 2021|language=Portuguese}}</ref> He averaged 6.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 10.5 [[Efficiency (basketball)|efficiency]] and 23.0 minutes on the court - at only 16 years of age.<ref name="Chacon">[https://www.olimpiadatododia.com.br/basquete/161055-confira-10-prospectos-que-disputarao-a-ldb-2019/ Confira 10 prospectos que disputarão a LDB 2019] {{in lang|pt}}. Paulo Chacon (Olimpiada Todo Dia). {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629121818/https://www.olimpiadatododia.com.br/basquete/161055-confira-10-prospectos-que-disputarao-a-ldb-2019/|date=29 June 2021}}, 10 July 2019. Accessed 23 June 2021.</ref> In the [[2018–19 NBB season]], because Santos was still in school and for several other reasons, he was unable to fully follow the adult team's routine.<ref name="Ottoni">Ottoni, Daniel (14 August 2020). [https://www.otempo.com.br/superfc/especializados/ala-gui-carvalho-prestes-a-ganhar-mais-espaco-no-basquete-do-minas-tenis-clube-1.2371659 Ala Gui Carvalho prestes a ganhar mais espaço no basquete do Minas Tênis Clube] {{in lang|pt}} {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603201909/https://www.otempo.com.br/superfc/especializados/ala-gui-carvalho-prestes-a-ganhar-mais-espaco-no-basquete-do-minas-tenis-clube-1.2371659|date=3 June 2021}}. Accessed 28 June 2021.</ref>

In the 2019 Basketball Development League (LDB), he was the leader of the Minas team. At 17, his averages were 14.5 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.6 assists in the U-20 championship.<ref name="Ottoni"/> In 2019, Santos was already part of his club's senior cast. He entered the court in three Minas games in the [[2018–19 NBB season]]—against [[Associação dos Amigos do Basquete de Joinville|Joinville]], [[Club de Regatas Vasco da Gama (basketball)|Vasco]] and [[Franca Basquetebol Clube|Sesi Franca]].<ref name="Chacon"/> In the [[2019–20 NBB season]], Minas' coach Léo Costa granted him a bigger role with the team.<ref name="Ottoni"/>

In April 2021, Santos was named to the World Team for the [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. On April 21, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Brazil's Gui Santos entering 2021 NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31302089|website=ESPN.com|date=21 April 2021|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref> In the 2021–22 season, Santos was named the NBB Sixth Man of the Year after he averaged 10.1 points and 5.1 rebounds over the season.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=BRUNO CABOCLO IS NAMED MVP OF THE 2021-22 NBB SEASON. CHECK OUT ALL THE AWARDS|url=https://www.streetopia.me/m/news/62ac842f9be04d64d3123cf5/bruno-caboclo-is-named-mvp-of-the-2021-22-nbb-season-check-out-all-the-awards|website=Streetopia.me|access-date=17 July 2022|date=17 June 2022|last=Sasso|first=Leonardo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Gui Santos Player Profile, Golden State Warriors, News, Stats - Eurobasket|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/index.aspx|website=EuroBasket.com|access-date=17 July 2022}}</ref>

On 3 September 2021, he scored a career-high 34 points for Minas' U20 team in a 72–77 away win over [[Flamengo Basketball|Flamengo]] U20.<ref>{{cite web|title=Regular Season Round 18: Flamengo - Minas 72-77|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/boxScores/Brazil/2021/0903_49318_49327.asp|website=LatinBasket.com|access-date=17 July 2022}}</ref>

===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2022–present)===
Santos was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 55th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Select Patrick Baldwin Jr. (#28) & Gui Santos (#55) in 2022 NBA Draft, Presented by Oracle|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-draft-results-20220623|website=NBA.com|date=23 June 2022|access-date=23 June 2022}}</ref> He joined the Warriors for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]], and he later joined their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]]. Santos was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=7 February 2023|access-date=8 March 2023}}</ref>

On 7 November 2023, Golden State signed Santos to a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Forward Gui Santos|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-forward-gui-santos-20231107|website=NBA.com|date=7 November 2023|access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref> Throughout the next two seasons, Santos was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to Santa Cruz.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Santa Cruz Warriors Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Santa-Cruz-Warriors/35/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=17 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Santa Cruz Warriors Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Santa-Cruz-Warriors/35/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=17 December 2024}}</ref> He made 23 appearances for the Warriors during his rookie campaign, averaging 3.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gui Santos 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4997536/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 15 January 2025, Santos made his first career start, tallying five points, three assists, and seven rebounds in a 116–115 victory over the [[2024–25 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Johnson | first=Dalton | title=How back of Warriors' bench gave them exactly what they needed | website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California | date=2025-01-16 | url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/gui-santos-pat-spencer-quinten-post-steve-kerr/1821508 | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> He made 52 appearances (including two starts) for the Warriors during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 4.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gui Santos 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4997536/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 29 June 2025, the Warriors exercised the team option for Santos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Exercise Team Options on Quinten Post and Gui Santos|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/quinten-post-gui-santos-team-options-exercised-20250629|website=NBA.com|date=June 29, 2025|access-date=June 29, 2025}}</ref> On 28 February 2026, Santos signed a three-year, $15 million contract extension with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Gui Santos to Multi-Year Contract Extension|url=https://warriors.com/news/warriors-sign-gui-santos-to-multi-year-contract-extension-20260228|website=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2026|access-date=February 28, 2026}}</ref> On 7 March, he recorded a career-high 22 points and 11 rebounds in a 97–104 loss to the [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gui Santos Scores Career-High 22 Points as Dubs Fall in Oklahoma City|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gameday-recap-20260307|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> In a 109–106 victory over the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]] on 25 March, Santos increased his career-high to 31 points, also logging three rebounds, two steals, one assist, and one block.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warriors' Gui Santos: Pours in career-high 31 in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-gui-santos-pours-in-career-high-31-in-win/|access-date=April 6, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Santos helped Brazil win gold at the 2019 [[FIBA South America Under-17 Championship for Men|FIBA South America Under-17 Championship]] in Chile. He scored 27 points against [[Argentina men's national under-17 basketball team|Argentina]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brazil claim South American U17 Championship 2019 title in Chile|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/u17sudamericano/2019/news/brazil-claim-south-american-u17-championship-2019-title-in-chile|website=FIBA.basketball|date=1 December 2019|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref> Santos made his [[Brazil men's national basketball team|senior national team]] debut during [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup qualification]].<ref name=massi>{{cite web|first=Luciano|last=Massi|title=Gui Santos, do Minas e Seleção Brasileira, comenta sobre grande fase no NBB 13|url=https://www.radiopoliesportiva.com.br/gui-santos-do-minas-e-selecao-brasileira-comenta-sobre-grande-fase-no-nbb-13/|website=RádioPoliesportiva.com.br|date=11 March 2021|access-date=3 June 2021|language=Portuguese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603185300/https://www.radiopoliesportiva.com.br/gui-santos-do-minas-e-selecao-brasileira-comenta-sobre-grande-fase-no-nbb-13/|archive-date=3 June 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2020, Santos was called up by [[Aleksandar Petrović (basketball, born February 1959)|Aleksandar Petrović]] for the [[Brazil men's national basketball team|Brazilian senior national team]]. He scored 11 points in the two games against [[Uruguay men's national basketball team|Uruguay]] at the 2021 Copa America qualifiers.<ref name="Ottoni"/>

==Miscellaneous==
Santos was one of the Brazilian representatives at [[Basketball Without Borders]], a camp held by [[FIBA]] and the [[NBA]] that brought together 64 prospects from Latin America for training sessions in the city of [[Medellín]] (Colombia), and also at the [[FIBA Americas]] Youth Elite Camp, that happened in [[Campinas]], Brazil at the end of 2018.<ref name="Chacon"/>

He recalls that especially the support of Minas teammates [[Alex Garcia (basketball)|Alex Garcia]] and [[Leandro Barbosa]], helped him shape his game and reach success.<ref name="Ottoni"/>

==Personal life==
Santos' father, Deivisson, is a former professional basketball player who played five seasons in the NBB.<ref name=massi/> His mother, Lucineide, was also a basketball player.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Leonardo|last1=Sasso|first2=Pedro|last2=Suaide|title=NBB: armador de 16 anos do Minas Tênis Clube joga por 3 categorias, brinca sobre ENEM e é desafiado por companheiros|url=https://www.espn.com.br/basquete/artigo/_/id/4974298|website=ESPN.com|date=13 November 2018|access-date=3 June 2021|language=pt|name-list-style=and}}</ref>
